section_hierarchy.title: SECTION 1. PREAMBLE, OPERATIONAL RECITALS, AND EXTENSIVE DEFINITIONS

content:
1.1 Contractual Preamble and Identification of Strategic Purpose
This Master Technology Risk, Revenue, Data, and Platform Governance Agreement is entered into by and between the
technology platform operator identified in the applicable execution record, ordering instrument, signed statement of work,
authenticated procurement record, or mutually accepted commercial schedule as the "Provider," and the enterprise
customer, institutional subscriber, commercial sponsor, or authorized system user identified in that same execution record as
the "Customer." Provider and Customer are each a "Party" and together are the "Parties." The Parties intend this Agreement
to function as a durable, comprehensive, and operationally enforceable governance instrument for advanced software
systems, retrieval-augmented generation environments, document intelligence pipelines, metadata extraction services, legal
analytics engines, model orchestration layers, secure processing nodes, and any related hosted, managed, licensed,
embedded, integrated, or professional services made available by or through Provider to Customer.
The Parties acknowledge that the systems covered by this Agreement may receive, ingest, classify, parse, normalize, chunk,
index, embed, retrieve, summarize, compare, transmit, store, transform, log, and otherwise process materials that may have
legal, financial, commercial, regulatory, operational, competitive, or reputational significance. The Parties further
acknowledge that the relationship governed by this Agreement is not a casual trial, consumer subscription, unsecured data
exchange, or informal technical collaboration. It is a controlled enterprise technology arrangement requiring disciplined
allocation of ownership rights, confidentiality obligations, data governance responsibilities, financial duties, security
commitments, audit mechanisms, liability boundaries, escalation pathways, and termination consequences.

section_hierarchy.title: SECTION 1. PREAMBLE, OPERATIONAL RECITALS, AND EXTENSIVE DEFINITIONS
1.1 Contractual Preamble and Identification of Strategic Purpose

content:
1.2 Operational Recitals
Provider represents that it operates or controls specialized technological infrastructure capable of supporting high-sensitivity
enterprise workflows, including document retrieval, contractual analysis, knowledge base augmentation, controlled
generation, structured extraction, permissions-aware search, and technical risk mitigation. Customer desires access to such
infrastructure for internal business, legal, compliance, financial, operational, or research purposes, subject to the restrictions,
safeguards, and commercial rules set forth in this Agreement. Provider is willing to make the contracted services available
only upon the condition that Customer observes strict limits on use, disclosure, reverse engineering, benchmarking, model
training, competitive derivation, and handling of confidential or regulated information.
Customer acknowledges that Provider's platform may include proprietary software, system architecture, technical
documentation, orchestration logic, algorithmic weights, prompts, guardrails, evaluation tooling, vector indexes, connectors,
processing methods, product roadmaps, support processes, and security configurations. Customer further acknowledges
that the economic value of the relationship depends not only upon access to visible user interfaces or outputs, but also upon
the preservation of Provider's hidden technical assets, confidential operational methods, commercial pricing structures,
usage telemetry, and non-public compliance controls. Provider acknowledges that Customer may contribute sensitive
documents, business instructions, regulated data, internal policies, matter files, customer records, procurement materials,
source materials, and proprietary analytical requirements, and that such Customer-controlled materials require protection
against unauthorized access, unauthorized disclosure, improper use, and uncontrolled retention.
The Parties therefore enter into this Agreement to establish a full-spectrum contractual framework that identifies the exact
legal consequences of access, payment, use, audit, security failure, tax treatment, intellectual property exposure, data
processing, breach response, indemnification, default, and dispute resolution. Each recital is intended to inform interpretation
of the operative provisions, and no recital shall be treated as mere surplusage where it clarifies the commercial purpose,
technical dependency, risk allocation, or intended boundary of a defined term.

content:
1.4 Definitions Matrix
#### 1.4.1 "Affiliates" "Affiliates" means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by,
or is under common Control with that Party at the relevant time. The term includes parent companies, subsidiaries, sister
companies, controlled joint ventures, controlled portfolio companies, successor entities, and entities operating through
contractual management arrangements where effective operational power is equivalent to ownership control. Affiliates do not
include independent contractors, ordinary suppliers, end customers, passive investors, lenders, franchisees, resellers, or
channel partners unless the applicable entity satisfies the Control test or is expressly designated in an ordering document.
Where an entity ceases to satisfy the Control test, it ceases to be an Affiliate prospectively, but obligations arising from
access, use, receipt of Confidential Information, or processing of Customer Data during the period of affiliation survive.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 1

content:
1.4.2 "Control"
"Control" means the direct or indirect power to direct or cause the direction of the management, policies, security posture,
financial decision-making, or operational conduct of an entity, whether through ownership of voting securities, contractual
rights, board appointment powers, management authority, veto rights over material decisions, or any comparable legal or
practical mechanism. Control is presumed where a person or entity owns more than fifty percent of the voting interests of
another entity, but may also exist below that threshold where governance rights provide decisive influence. Control does not
arise from ordinary minority investor protections, non-exclusive commercial influence, technical integration, or standard
vendor management rights unless those rights allow actual direction of strategic or operational conduct. A change of Control
includes merger, consolidation, sale of substantially all assets, transfer of controlling voting interests, or other transaction by
which a new person obtains controlling power.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 1

content:
1.4.3 "Services"
"Services" means all hosted services, managed services, licensed software access, APIs, integrations, support functions,
implementation assistance, analytics features, administrative dashboards, documentation, professional services,
maintenance releases, security tooling, and related deliverables made available by Provider under this Agreement. The term
includes production services, sandbox services, beta modules, preview functions, staging environments, support portals,
reporting interfaces, and any system component that is technically necessary for Customer to receive the contracted
functionality. Services exclude third-party platforms not controlled by Provider, Customer systems, Customer-provided data
repositories, telecommunications networks, internet access, and any optional functionality not ordered or expressly enabled
for Customer.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 1

content:
1.4.4 "Intellectual Property Rights"
"Intellectual Property Rights" means all patents, patent applications, copyrights, database rights, design rights, mask work
rights, trade secret rights, moral rights to the extent waivable, trademark rights, service mark rights, domain name rights,
know-how rights, confidential information rights, rights in inventions, rights in algorithms, rights in source code and object
code, rights in technical documentation, and all similar proprietary rights existing anywhere in the world. The term includes
applications, registrations, renewals, extensions, continuations, divisionals, reissues, improvements, enhancements,
derivative works, and goodwill associated with protected subject matter. Intellectual Property Rights do not include a mere
contractual license to use another person's technology except to the extent that the license itself is an enforceable
contractual right. No transfer of Intellectual Property Rights occurs by implication, course of dealing, access to a system,
delivery of an output, payment of fees, or technical interoperability.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 1

content:
1.4.5 "Customer Data"
"Customer Data" means all documents, prompts, records, communications, attachments, instructions, datasets, matter
materials, financial records, legal files, user inputs, configuration choices, annotations, metadata intentionally supplied by
Customer, and other information submitted to or made available through the Services by or on behalf of Customer. Customer
Data includes data submitted by Customer's authorized users, Affiliates, administrators, agents, and integrated systems.
Customer Data excludes Provider technology, System Metadata, aggregated operational statistics that do not identify

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 2

content:
1.4.6 "System Metadata"
"System Metadata" means technical, operational, administrative, and diagnostic information generated by the Services
concerning use, performance, security, configuration, availability, error states, resource consumption, routing, access events,
processing latency, feature interaction, authentication activity, and service health. The term includes timestamps, IP-derived
connection data, tenant identifiers, session identifiers, API request counts, error logs, event logs, queue data, processing
durations, token counts, storage metrics, node routing records, audit trails, and administrative actions. System Metadata
does not include the substantive content of Customer Data except to the extent such content appears unavoidably within
limited log fragments needed for debugging, security investigation, legal compliance, or incident response. Provider may use
System Metadata to operate, secure, improve, support, and audit the Services, provided that such use remains subject to
confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 2

content:
1.4.7 "Core Algorithmic Weights"
"Core Algorithmic Weights" means the numerical parameters, learned representations, trained coefficients, embeddings,
model checkpoints, gradient-derived values, attention structures, transformer parameters, vector-space components, ranking
parameters, calibration values, and other non-public machine-learned artifacts that influence the behavior of an artificial
intelligence model or retrieval system controlled by Provider. The term includes base model weights, fine-tuned weights,
adapter layers, reinforcement learning artifacts, evaluation-tuned weights, reranker weights, and any model component that
can materially alter generation, retrieval, classification, scoring, routing, or summarization. Core Algorithmic Weights do not
include Customer Data merely because it is processed by a model, nor do they include general ideas observable from
ordinary use of the Services. Customer receives no right to inspect, copy, export, reconstruct, benchmark for replication, or
derive Core Algorithmic Weights.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 2

content:
1.4.8 "Processing Nodes"
"Processing Nodes" means the logical or physical computing resources, containers, virtual machines, serverless functions,
orchestration workers, queue consumers, storage processors, inference endpoints, indexing workers, embedding services,
database instances, cache layers, or other execution environments used to receive, process, transform, retrieve, store, route,
or transmit data in connection with the Services. Processing Nodes may operate in production, staging, failover, backup, test,
support, or disaster recovery environments. The term includes nodes operated directly by Provider and nodes operated by
approved Sub-processors under Provider's control. A Processing Node is not deemed transferred, leased, or dedicated to
Customer merely because it processes Customer Data or appears in a tenant-specific workflow, unless an ordering
document expressly provides for dedicated infrastructure.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 2

content:
1.4.9 "Service Level Agreement" or "SLA"
"Service Level Agreement" or "SLA" means the written commitments governing availability, uptime, support response,
severity classification, incident escalation, maintenance windows, recovery objectives, performance thresholds, service
credits, and measurement exclusions applicable to the Services. An SLA is measured only against the production services
expressly covered by the applicable ordering document and excludes beta features, customer-side failures, force majeure
interruptions, scheduled maintenance, emergency maintenance, third-party network failures outside Provider's reasonable
control, unauthorized use, or interruptions caused by Customer's systems, credentials, instructions, integrations, or breach.
SLA credits, where expressly stated, constitute a measured financial adjustment and not an admission of fault, warranty
failure, indemnifiable event, or liquidated damages unless the Agreement expressly states otherwise.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 2

content:
1.4.10 "Sub-processors"
"Sub-processors" means third-party service providers, cloud infrastructure operators, hosting providers, security vendors,
support tools, analytics processors, payment processors, professional service providers, or other entities engaged by
Provider to process Customer Data or personal data on Provider's behalf in connection with the Services. Sub-processors do
not include telecommunications carriers, internet backbone providers, domain name services, or public network operators
that merely transmit data without selecting or determining processing purposes. Provider remains responsible for the acts
and omissions of Sub-processors to the extent required by this Agreement and applicable law. Provider shall impose written
obligations on Sub-processors that are no less protective in material respects than the confidentiality, security, and data

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content:
1.4.11 "Confidential Information"
"Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party to the other Party, whether
orally, visually, electronically, physically, or by access to systems, that is identified as confidential or that reasonably should
be understood to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. The term includes business plans,
financial terms, pricing, security documentation, audit reports, product roadmaps, technical architecture, source code, APIs,
credentials, vulnerability information, customer lists, legal strategies, data processing details, usage information, Customer
Data, Provider technology, model behavior specifications, compliance materials, and non-public negotiations. Confidential
Information excludes information that the receiving Party can prove was lawfully known without restriction before disclosure,
independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's information, publicly available through no breach, or lawfully
received from a third party without confidentiality restriction.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content:
1.4.12 "Force Majeure Events"
"Force Majeure Events" means events beyond a Party's reasonable control that prevent or materially delay performance
despite commercially reasonable mitigation efforts. The term may include natural disasters, fire, flood, earthquake, epidemic,
pandemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest, government action, embargo, labor disruption not limited to the affected Party's own
workforce, internet backbone failure, utility failure, cloud provider regional outage, denial-of-service attack, or sudden legal
prohibition. Force Majeure Events do not include lack of funds, ordinary changes in market conditions, failure to maintain
reasonable backups, failure to implement known security controls, foreseeable supplier failure without contingency planning,
or a Party's internal operational mismanagement. Payment obligations for amounts already accrued are not excused by force
majeure except where payment systems are legally or technically unavailable.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content:
1.4.13 "Covered Loss"
"Covered Loss" means damages, liabilities, penalties, settlement amounts, judgments, awards, fines, costs, expenses,
reasonable attorneys' fees, expert fees, investigation costs, remediation costs, notification expenses, forensic expenses, and
other legally recoverable losses that fall within an indemnity, reimbursement, liquidated damages, or liability allocation
provision of this Agreement. Covered Loss excludes amounts that are speculative, punitive, exemplary, indirect, or
consequential unless the relevant provision expressly includes them or applicable law does not permit exclusion. Covered
Loss may include regulatory fines, third-party claims, data subject claims, intellectual property infringement losses, breach
notification costs, and reasonable technical remediation costs where the triggering clause expressly covers the relevant
event.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content:
1.4.14 "Gross Negligence"
"Gross Negligence" means a severe departure from the standard of care that a reasonable enterprise technology provider,
enterprise customer, officer, security professional, or system administrator would exercise under comparable circumstances,
reflecting reckless disregard for a known or obvious risk of material harm. Gross Negligence requires more than ordinary
error, isolated mistake, reasonable technical judgment that proves incorrect, or failure to achieve a perfect outcome. It
includes conscious failure to follow known mandatory safeguards, deliberate disregard of critical security alerts, knowingly
operating exposed credentials, failing to contain a confirmed compromise, or ignoring a known defect likely to cause
substantial loss. Whether conduct constitutes Gross Negligence must be evaluated in light of the information reasonably
available at the time, not solely through hindsight.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content:
1.4.15 "Material Breach"
"Material Breach" means a breach that substantially defeats the commercial, technical, confidentiality, security, payment,
intellectual property, data protection, or risk-allocation purpose of this Agreement. Material Breach includes non-payment
after required notice, unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information, prohibited reverse engineering, misuse of outputs
for model training, intentional circumvention of access controls, unlawful processing of regulated data, repeated SLA failures
not excused by the Agreement, failure to cooperate with breach response, infringement of Intellectual Property Rights, or
violation of audit obligations. A breach may be material even if monetary damages are difficult to quantify, particularly where
the breach threatens confidentiality, platform integrity, regulatory compliance, technical secrecy, or customer trust.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 3

content: 1.4.16 "Authorized Users"

"Authorized Users" means Customer's employees, officers, contractors, legal advisors, technical administrators, and
approved Affiliate personnel who are permitted by Customer to access the Services under Customer's account and for whom
Customer remains responsible. Authorized Users must access the Services only through valid credentials, approved
authentication methods, and assigned permission levels. Customer shall not permit credential sharing, anonymous access,
unmanaged shared accounts, or use by persons who are not subject to confidentiality and acceptable-use obligations. Acts
and omissions of Authorized Users are deemed acts and omissions of Customer for purposes of this Agreement.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 4

content:
1.4.17 "Output"
"Output" means text, classifications, summaries, scores, citations, extracted fields, recommendations, reports, comparisons,
structured data, metadata displays, search results, generated language, or other materials produced by the Services in
response to Customer Data, prompts, queries, configurations, or workflow actions. Output may be probabilistic,
confidence-ranked, incomplete, or dependent on source material quality. Unless expressly stated, Output is not legal advice,
tax advice, financial advice, professional judgment, or a substitute for human review. Customer is responsible for validating
Output before relying on it in legal, regulatory, financial, employment, procurement, safety, or other consequential decisions.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 4

content:
1.4.18 "Security Incident"
"Security Incident" means an event that Provider confirms has resulted in unauthorized access to, acquisition of, exfiltration
of, disclosure of, alteration of, destruction of, or loss of control over Customer Data or systems used to process Customer
Data. Security Incident does not include unsuccessful intrusion attempts, port scans, pings, automated attacks blocked by
security controls, or events affecting only anonymized data, provided that no Customer Data was compromised. A Security
Incident may arise from malicious conduct, credential compromise, system misconfiguration, unauthorized employee activity,
Sub-processor failure, or external attack. The classification of an event as a Security Incident does not by itself determine
fault, breach, damages, or indemnity.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 4

content:
1.4.19 "Applicable Law"
"Applicable Law" means all statutes, regulations, directives, rules, binding regulatory guidance, court orders, sanctions laws,
export control laws, tax laws, privacy laws, cybersecurity laws, digital services laws, anti-corruption laws, and other legally
enforceable requirements applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement. Applicable Law includes laws of
jurisdictions in which the Services are provided, Customer Data is processed, payments are made, personnel are located,
regulatory obligations attach, or legal claims are asserted. Each Party is responsible for identifying and complying with laws
applicable to its own business, systems, users, and instructions, except where this Agreement expressly assigns a particular
compliance duty to the other Party.

section_hierarchy.title: Section 1 - Preamble, Operational Recitals, and Extensive Definitions Matrix | Page 4

content:
1.5 Interpretive Priority
In the event of conflict, the signed ordering document controls solely with respect to pricing, purchased quantities,
subscription term, and expressly identified business-specific deviations; this Agreement controls with respect to intellectual
property, confidentiality, data security, privacy, prohibited uses, liability allocation, audit, remedies, governing law, and
dispute resolution unless the ordering document states the exact clause being modified and the specific replacement
language. No purchase order, invoice note, online portal term, procurement acknowledgement, or unilateral vendor form
shall modify this Agreement unless signed by authorized legal representatives of both Parties.
